found: Trove now takes makers and providers in Sharjah too, but every post said "Dubai and Abu Dhabi".
Post 2's name tags missed the crafts Trove most wants: jewellery, crochet and painting. Its caption and the manifesto still had the wedding-card lettering line.
Every slide used the same greens, neutrals, linen and wood, so on the grid the posts blurred into one.
Nearly every piece shown was a neutral ceramic or oatmeal linen. A maker whose work is bright, patterned or traditional would think Trove isn't for them.
Owner, 26 Oct: the first dates have passed, and there should be more images and video, less text.
changed: New calendar: Sat 31 Oct to Sat 28 Nov, every two or three days at 18:30 Dubai time, in the same order. The buyers Reel moves to Wed 2 Dec, UAE National Day, only if the Marketplace is open to buyers by then.
Eight of fourteen posts are Reels. Posts 3 (Makers. Providers. Buyers.), 5 (You make it. Trove sells it.) and 8 (workshops) became Reels; every Reel has five shots of hands at work (post 2 has six).

Carousels are photo-led: one headline and one short line per photo, about twelve words at most. The steps, lists and Q&As moved into the captions. Post 9 went from eight slides to seven, post 6 from five to four.
Maker and provider posts say Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. Buyer posts keep Dubai and Abu Dhabi, where deliveries go. #SharjahMakers joins the hashtags.
Post 2's five name tags follow the feedback (earrings, blanket, cushion cover, painting, heirloom chair), each in its own style, and the Reel ends on the one-liner.
Each post has a lead colour and each carousel one colour family. Colour sits in the band under each photo; the offer and the 60% sit on Charcoal; end cards are always Cream.

25 new images show every kind of maker: pearl earrings, a pastel blanket, terracotta and indigo embroidery, an abstract painting, cobalt plates, jewel-toned beads, a crocheted toy, a dog collar, a kintsugi bowl, a mural, a kids' craft party. Hands of different ages, skin tones and genders.
"Any style. Made by hand." on post 3, at the start of post 4's caption and as post 12's last line.
Diwali (Sun 8 Nov) and Downtown Design (4 to 8 Nov) move to Stories: the maker posts come first, so the provider post can't fall on Diwali.
declined: Pure colour type cards between photos (the feedback's "photo, card, photo, card"): your 21 Oct rule is no slide without a photo, and today's ask is less text. The colour goes in the band under each photo instead.
Ajman, Al Ain and the "apply anyway" line for other emirates: not added until you decide.
Dream Avenue headlines: Cormorant stays. You chose it on 27 July because Dream Avenue was never bought. The wordmark still swaps in when the file arrives.
Cutting services to workshops, styling and photography: lettering, repairs, gift wrapping and the rest are real categories on the site. Covers lead with three; the inside keeps the range.
"Free to join. Keep 60%." as a headline: your 19 Oct rule keeps money out of headlines. Post 9 keeps "What Trove costs, and what you keep." and the 60% stays inside.
"In a world of fast, throwaway things": the brief never knocks mass-made goods. The line is now "Pieces made with care, by people you can name."
"Handmade homeware" in the one-liner: Trove also takes jewellery, stationery, children's and pet pieces, so it says "handmade pieces".
Kiln & Clay: it was a test shop, removed from the live site on 15 Oct, and it isn't in any post.

campaign.manifesto:
Some of us were born here. Some of us came from far away.
Either way, home is something we make.
A pair of earrings, made for a bride.
A blanket, crocheted for a new baby.
A cushion cover, stitched by hand.
A painting, made for a first home.
An heirloom chair, brought back to life.
Here, home is made by hand: by neighbours, by friends, by people you can name.
Trove is a new online marketplace for handmade pieces and creative services in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.
We take the photographs. A courier comes to your door. You keep making.
Made here. Made home.

outreach: American University of Sharjah, College of Architecture, Art and Design; University of Sharjah, College of Fine Arts and Design. Degree shows and student societies first. Makers must be 18 or over, and students on a student visa may need a permit to earn (business adviser, before any student outreach).
Irthi Contemporary Crafts Council, Sharjah Art Foundation, Maraya Art Centre (VERIFY each, and ask before approaching their artists or makers).
Weekend and seasonal craft markets in Sharjah (VERIFY names and dates before listing them): walk them like the Dubai and Abu Dhabi markets, and DM stallholders afterwards.

Downtown Design (4 to 8 Nov, d3, VERIFY on downtowndesign.com and check its rules on approaching exhibitors), weekend craft markets, Tashkeel and Alserkal Avenue in Dubai, Warehouse421 in Abu Dhabi (VERIFY each).
A Stories series once a real student maker has applied and agreed: same terms as every other maker. Make pausing a shop easy around exams.

posts.drives: Understanding what Trove is, then applications
posts.caption: Trove is a new online marketplace for handmade pieces and creative services in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah. Makers sell what they make by hand, in any style: jewellery, ceramics, prints, textiles, candles, children's pieces and more. Providers take bookings for workshops, home styling and photography. Makers join free, and providers list free during launch. We photograph your pieces, or you use your own, and a courier collects each sale from your door. Make something, or offer a service? Apply in about ten minutes at troveathome.com/apply. Looking to buy? Follow along: the Marketplace opens to buyers soon.

posts.for: People who make things by hand, including those who have never sold
posts.caption: Any style. Made by hand. If you make things by hand, you're a maker, whether you've sold a hundred pieces or none: pearl earrings or bright beadwork, quiet ceramics or bold prints, toys, collars and cards. shoot.intro: Book it before the first posts go out: every cover and Reel uses Higgsfield stand-ins until real hands replace them, and post 10 needs a real founding maker. v6 adds three scenes for post 2's new name tags (14 to 16). Ask the people filmed to bring their own work in any style, bright and patterned as well as quiet. One afternoon, 14:00 to dusk, in two homes (an apartment and a villa, or a home and its building corridor). Three or four consenting friends, family or team members who genuinely make or mend things, using their real craft. They are never presented as Trove makers; the only credit is "Filmed with friends of Trove at home in [area]". Offer hands-only to everyone up front.
